newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercial, exporter buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercial, exporter buying.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on commercial and exporter demand, supported by gains in Chicago's soycomplex, traders said.

"LFG's the best buyer, XCan was a late buyer. There's commercial and exporter demand. Cargill sold November," a trader said. Two hundred May-July spread at even money, Jan Mar at $0.50, Nov-Mar at $5.30 and Nov-July at $6. Volume was 4,335 lots, or 86,700, with 225 hedge lots.
Japan bought 2,000-3,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
November canola rose $4.40 to $439.10, January up $3.60 to $442.70. October flax fell $5.50 to $394.50 on commercials.
October feed wheat rose $2 at $199, December lost $0.20 to $184.50 on commercial hedge sales, commission short covering. Volume was 1,535 lots. Oats did not trade.
November western barley closed $0.10 higher at $150.20 and February was up $0.60 at $154.90 on commercial short covering. Nov-Feb spread at $4. Volume was 1,350 lots.
UGG sold October and December peas down US$0.50 to US$209.50 and US$211, respectively, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, peas)
